title: openai-compat: map tool schemas and support tool_choice + tool message formatting
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds OpenAI-compatible tool schema mapping, supports tool_choice events in streaming, and normalizes tool message formatting for consistent downstream handling. Backwards-compatible with existing Redwood tool APIs.
description:
Context: Customers building against the OpenAI function/tool calling surface expect a predictable mapping from our internal 'tool' APIs to OpenAI-compatible 'functions' JSON Schema and streaming semantics (including partial/tool_choice events).

This PR implements a compatibility layer that: 1) maps Redwood tool metadata to OpenAI 'functions' entries (name, description, parameters JSON Schema), 2) normalizes our tool message envelopes so clients see consistent assistant/tool messages, and 3) implements streaming 'tool_choice' delta events so clients can detect that the model is selecting a tool before the tool output is returned.

Motivation: recent customer requests and compatibility tests surfaced mismatches in parameter shaping and streaming deltas (see ENG-3241).

Changes made:
- Add a schema mapper that converts Redwood tool definitions (typed parameters, enum variants, nested structs) into OpenAI-style JSON Schema Function entries. The mapper includes heuristics to preserve required fields, nullable handling, and custom types via fallback to string.
- Introduce a ToolMessage format in the OpenAI compat layer: assistant messages that represent a tool call are emitted as role=\"assistant\" with content empty and tool_call metadata; when a tool returns output we emit a role=\"tool\" message with name and content set to a normalized string payload.
- Streaming: implement tool_choice events as a distinct delta type on the stream. Clients receive a streaming assistant delta with {\"tool_choice\": {\"name\": \"<tool>\", \"arguments_partial\": \"...\"}} followed by either tool output or assistant finish. This mirrors OpenAI's partial tool selection semantics and lets clients render 'invoking tool' UI.
- Backwards compatibility shims so existing Redwood clients (non-OpenAI consumers) continue to receive the previous internal tool event format.
- Tests: unit coverage for schema mapping edge cases (enums, nullable arrays, nested objects), integration test verifying streaming tool_choice sequence end-to-end, and a small load test ensuring mapper CPU overhead is negligible under 500 rps.

Commits:
- Add schema mapper and mapper unit tests
- Implement streaming tool_choice delta handling in compat stream layer
- Normalize tool message envelope and add compatibility shims
- Add integration tests and update docs
- Fix edge case for nullable enums and add comments

Files changed (high level):
- packages/openai-compat/src/mapper.ts (main mapping logic + tests)
- packages/openai-compat/src/streaming.ts (stream delta encoding for tool_choice)
- packages/server/src/tool-routing.ts (compat shim hooks)
- packages/sdk-js/src/compat.ts (client-facing envelope normalization)
- docs/openai-compat.md (documentation + examples)
- test/integration/tool-stream-e2e.test.ts
- test/unit/mapper.test.ts
- changelogs/CHANGELOG.md (entry)

Review notes and discussion summary:
- Diego: requested clearer handling for nullable enums and explicit fallback rules. Implemented and added tests.
- Logan: asked to ensure streaming bandwidth was not bloated by verbose schema JSON on every call; moved heavy schema payload to an initial manifest event when possible.
- Priya: requested doc examples demonstrating how existing Redwood tool consumers get the same message shape. Added example and compatibility notes.

CI and checks:
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration e2e: pass
- Lint/typecheck: pass
- Load smoke: pass

Merge: Squash merged into main after approvals and CI green. Related linear tasks: ENG-3241 (compat mapping), ENG-3302 (streaming tool_choice), small follow-up ENG-3367 (doc clarifications).
